title: Cognitive Bias Modification for Interpretation (CBM-I) Training for Anxiety Disorders (Study A) and Posttraumatic Stress Disorder (Study B): A Randomized-Controlled Smartphone-App Based Trial.
summary: The presented study investigates Cognitive Bias Modification for Interpretation (CBM-I) within patients diagnosed with anxiety disorders or posttraumatic stress disorder. Cognitive models for anxiety and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) postulate that the respective disorder is maintained due to   dysfunctional cognitions and biased interpretations (e.g. MacLeod et al., 2009, Woud et al., 2017, Ehlers & Clark, 2000), thus indicating the necessity to treat interpretation biases to reduce symptom severity. During previous studies interpretation biases were mostly treated by means of a digital program referring to as CBM, however, findings were mixed regarding their effectivity (e.g. Würtz et al., 2022; Woud et al., 2017). Moreover results showed solely small to medium effect sizes (Liu et al. 2017, Sun et al.,2019, Vermeulen et al.,2019, Would et al., 2017). These problems could be due to the applied method (completion of sentences, short written scenarios), the amount of participants, or the study design (e.g., only one training sequence). The present study takes these methodological issues into account by using a Smartphone-App based CBM-I training, which contains disorder-specific imaginative audioscripts. These the content of these scripts evolves around typical disorder-specific situational interpretation biases, with each scenario being resolved in a positive fashion. Additionally, the training will be conducted three times a week over the course of three weeks. Specifically, in Study A the participants will be confronted with anxiety provoing situations, which will be resolved positively. In Study B patients diagnosed with PTSD will be presented with disorder-specific negatively assiociated situations (based on the PTCI), which will include cognitive biases related to negative perspectives of the self, others, and the world. The overall objective in Study A & B is the reduction of interpretation biases caused by anxiety disorders and PTSD. In Study C, the Scrambled Sentence Test (SST; Viviani et al., 2018) shall be established and validated for anxiety disorders, for the use within the German context. Both, healthy participants as well as clinical patients suffering from anxiety disorders will be included. Within study part D, the Identification with the Aggressor Scale (IAS; Lahav, Talmon & Ginzburg (2019)) for PTSD will be translated into German and established and validated for use within the German context including healthy participants as well as patients with PTSD.
conditions: Agoraphobia without history of panic disorder

interventions.name:
Part A: intervention group: CBM-I for anxiety disorder.
Waiting list control group: TAU. Upon study completing patients within the WL group will be able to access the CBM-I training.

Part B: intervention group: CBM-I for post-traumatic stress disorder.
Waiting list control group: TAU. Upon study completing patients within the WL group will be able to access the CBM-I training.
Part C: healthy control group without intervention, and patients with an anxiety disorder from Study A.
Part D: healthy control group without intervention, and patients with a post-traumatic stress disorder from Study B.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Diagnosis of anxiety disorder or phobic disorder (Study A);
Diagnosis of post-traumatic stress disorder (Study B); healthy subjects or subjects with anxiety disorder (Study C); healthy subjects or subjects with post-traumatic stress disorder (Study D).
Required age of 18years old.
German fluent in word an writing.
Exclusion criteria:
Ongoing psychotherapy, acute psychopharmacological emercency medication, severe comorbid disorders from the schizophrenic spectrum and bipolar-affective disorders, acute suicidality, addiction disorders
